news.title: Uefa maintains World Cup boycott still stands despite Fifa’s backing for Infantino
news.lede: European body says Fifa statement ‘changes nothing’. Fifpro condemns ‘profound abuse of presidential power’. Uefa has doubled down on its threat to boycott Fifa-run competitions and reiterated its loss of confidence in Gianni Infantino’s presidency. The latest damning intervention from European football’s governing body came as criticism of Infantino continued to rain in from several angles.

news.title: Uefa planning to check if Infantino tried to sell stakes in World Cup on cheap
news.lede: European body to commission independent valuation. Uefa unmoved by Infantino apology for ‘mistake’. Uefa plans to commission an independent valuation of Fifa’s World Cup sale plans after concerns that Gianni Infantino agreed to sell the tournament’s future profits to a private equity firm at below the market rate. The European governing body is unmoved by the written apology issued by Infantino to Fifa’s 211 member associations on Tuesday after crisis talks in Morocco.

news.title: Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller thinks MLS has gained prestige because of the World Cup
news.lede: In his personal monthly newspaper, Bayern Munich legend Thomas Müller spoke about the upcoming MLS season and what he’s been focused on these last few weeks. In it, he included hope that the World Cup and an influx of new star players has helped MLS raise its profile on the global stage. “I’m really burning to be on the pitch for 90 minutes regularly and help my lads with everything I’ve got,” wrote Müller. “We have six games in three weeks.

news.title: Gianni Infantino offered shock lifeline as under-fire FIFA chief's World Cup final plan pays off
news.lede: The Confederation of African Football executive committee has "unanimously reconfirmed" support in Gianni Infantino , after widespread calls for the FIFA president to lose his job. The 56-year-old executive sparked outrage last week with proposals to sell a stake of the World Cup to private investors. The move, which was dubbed the 'FIFA Forward Enterprise' was swiftly met with widespread criticism, with UEFA vowing to boycott the tournament outright should plans have proceeded. The backlash ultimately prompted Infantino to shelve his proposals, which he dubbed to be an act of consolation rather than concrete plans that World Football were planning on rolling out.

news.title: UEFA maintains World Cup boycott threat despite FIFA push to end internal turmoil
news.lede: FIFA's bid to move past the biggest internal crisis of Gianni Infantino's presidency is unlikely to end scrutiny of how world soccer is governed, with UEFA saying on Thursday that it remained committed to boycotting the World Cup. A day after FIFA's leadership gathered in Rabat to publicly reaffirm support for Infantino, the world governing body apologised to its 211 members for mistakes around the abandoned proposal to sell a slice of the World Cup's commercial future. FIFA also pledged to review the processes that led to the controversy that sparked the fiercest revolt of Infantino's tenure after national federations complained they had been sidelined. In a statement issued after Wednesday's meeting, FIFA acknowledged that the proposal "should have been handled differently" and said it was not their intention for the FIFA Council or associations to feel excluded from the process.

news.title: Money, politics, and the ‘beautiful game’: FIFA battles to win back trust
news.lede: Americans know it as soccer. For hundreds of millions of people across the globe, it’s football. It’s what Brazilian superstar Pelé famously called “the beautiful game.” But now, the beautiful game is mired in an ugly battle involving big money and power politics.

news.title: Why Ranjit Bajaj is set to walk away from India's U-15 World Cup project
news.lede: The All India Football Federation’s latest move involving India’s U-15 team has run into trouble almost as quickly as it was announced. Barely hours after the federation named Ranjit Bajaj as manager of the India U-15 side for the FIFA U-15 World Cup in Azerbaijan, the Minerva Academy owner has decided against taking up the role.The appointment had followed weeks of debate around India’s youth football setup. While Bibiano Fernandes retained his position as head coach, the AIFF brought in Bajaj as team manager in what appeared to be an attempt to bring together one of the country’s most vocal grassroots advocates alongside its existing youth setup. Speaking exclusively to India Today, however, Bajaj revealed that he had not been informed about the appointment before it was made public.“.

news.title: UEFA Maintains World Cup Boycott Threat After Gianni Infantino's Crisis Meeting
news.lede: European soccer's governing body has retained its threat to boycott FIFA competitions despite FIFA apologizing for its failed plan to sell stakes in the World Cup.
